ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, a small ball is thrown horizontally from point $A$ at the top of an inclined plane with height $h$ at a speed of $v_{0}$. The ball lands at point $B$ at the bottom of the inclined plane (given the gravitational acceleration $g$, and neglecting air resistance). Find:

1. The time it takes for the small ball to travel from being thrown to landing at point $B$
2. The speed of the small ball when it reaches point $B$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the small ball is located at point A in the upper left, and the vertical height h is marked beside point A; point B is in the lower right. A straight inclined plane extends from A downward to the right to B, indicating that the small ball finally falls to the bottom end B of the inclined plane. At point A there is an initial-velocity arrow horizontally to the right, labeled v_0; the dashed trajectory starts from A and curves downward to the right to B, indicating the trajectory of horizontal projectile motion. Reasoning: According to the specified method, take the x-axis horizontal and the y-axis vertically downward. The small ball is thrown horizontally from A, so the initial vertical velocity v_{y0}=0. The vertical height difference from A to B is h, so the vertical displacement satisfies h=\frac{1}{2}gt^2. Solving gives the flight time t=\sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}}. When reaching B, the vertical velocity v_y=gt=g\sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}}=\sqrt{2gh}; there is no acceleration in the horizontal direction, so the horizontal velocity remains v_x=v_0. The magnitude of the resultant velocity is v=\sqrt{v_x^2+v_y^2}=\sqrt{v_0^2+2gh}.
